verdict.rationale: Godot's MIT license and 'free for any purpose' policy (godot-gh-2, godot-docs-16) mean there's no vendor lock-in, and the asset pipeline docs show raw source assets live in the project folder while only imported caches sit in a hidden .godot folder (godot-docs-9, godot-docs-17), implying user data stays in accessible files. However, there's no explicit documentation of a dedicated 'export all your data' or project-portability feature, nor confirmation that all internal formats (e.g. binary .tscn/.res variants) are fully open/documented. Missing for 10: explicit docs on project file format openness/portability guarantees, a documented data-export or migration tool, and independent corroboration that users can fully extract and reuse their data outside Godot.
